tool.excerpt: General elections took place in Moldova's autonomous region of Gagauzia on 15 November 2026 to elect the region's Governor (Gagauz: Başkan) and the members of Gagauzia's local parliament, the People's Assembly of Gagauzia. The move brought to an end a legislative deadlock in the region following the conviction of the previous governor, Evghenia Guțul, who received a seven-year sentence over illegal financing related to the outlawed Șor Party. On 21 September, Grigorii Uzun, a member of the Party of Socialists of the Republic of Moldova (PSRM), announced that he would not run in the election for the post of governor. This was despite him having been considered the PSRM's likeliest candidate, with Uzun being who ran in the 2023 gubernatorial election in the second round against Guțul. His announcement was due to the fact that he did not speak Romanian ("Moldovan", as he called it) at the time, as new provisions had been adopted in the electoral code in August requiring candidates for the post to speak both Gagauz and Romanian. Subsequently, on 24 September, the PSRM announced it would back Fiodor Gagauz, who submitted his registration documents to run as a candidate for governorship on the same day. tool.excerpt: General elections took place in Moldova's autonomous region of Gagauzia on 15 November 2026 to elect the region's Governor (Gagauz: Başkan) and the members of Gagauzia's local parliament, the People's Assembly of Gagauzia. The move brought to an end a legislative deadlock in the region following the conviction of the previous governor, Evghenia Guțul, who received a seven-year sentence over illegal financing related to the outlawed Șor Party. On 21 September, Grigorii Uzun, a member of the Party of Socialists of the Republic of Moldova (PSRM), announced that he would not run in the election for the post of governor. This was despite him having been considered the PSRM's likeliest candidate, with Uzun being who ran in the 2023 gubernatorial election in the second round against Guțul. His announcement was due to the fact that he did not speak Romanian ("Moldovan", as he called it) at the time, as new provisions had been adopted in the electoral code in August requiring candidates for the post to speak both Gagauz and Romanian. Subsequently, on 24 September, the PSRM announced it would back Fiodor Gagauz, who submitted his registration documents to run as a candidate for governorship on the same day. sentences: Până acum, și-au mai anunțat intenția de a candida Fiodor Gagauz, fost deputat în Parlament, Alexandr Stoianoglo, fost procuror general și actual deputat al fracțiunii „Alternativa”, precum și fostul deputat Petr Vlah.

Liderul organizației teritoriale a Partidului Socialiștilor a anunțat într-o conferință de presă că a luat această decizie întrucât nu cunoaște „limba moldovenească”, în contextul în care noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral, adoptate în august, obligă candidații să cunoască limbile română și găgăuză.

La o conferință de presă susținută alături de liderul partidului, Igor Dodon, parlamentarul a acuzat majoritatea parlamentară că a modificat intenționat, cu puțin timp înainte de alegeri, Codul electoral, introducând o normă care limitează participarea la scrutin a persoanelor care nu vorbesc limba de stat.
Am luat decizia de a nu-mi depune candidatura la alegerile pentru funcția de bașcan”, a declarat Uzun, care a criticat noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral.
Igor Dodon a mai declarat, că modificarea legislației electorale cu doar două săptămâni înainte de perioada electorală este contrară Constituției și practicilor europene.
Condiția privind cunoașterea limbii trebuia să fie introdusă începând cu următorul ciclu electoral, peste patru ani”, a afirmat Dodon.
Scrutinele se vor desfășura după noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral al Republicii Moldova, întrucât Codul Electoral al autonomiei nu mai este valabil.
În listele electorale din regiune sunt înscriși în jur de 129.000 de alegători.

But with the elections widely considered by the opposition and observers to have been rigged, the CEC meeting was marred by brawls and citizens protested outside the building. Shortly after the start of the meeting, Davit Kirtadze , the representative of the opposition Unity-UNM in the CEC, confronted the CEC Chair, Giorgi Kalandarishvili , calling him a “black spot” and splashing black paint on his face. This act was apparently a reference to the alleged violation of the ballot secrecy in the elections, in particular the issue of thin ballot papers which made it visible from the outside which party a citizen was voting for. Executive Summary The Nuclear Security Briefing Book (NSBB) was originally published as a reference guide on the international nuclear security framework for participants attending the Nuclear Security Summits (NSS), 2010-16. It has subsequently been expanded to include the post-NSS period, ensuring it remains a useful resource for policymakers, officials, practitioners, academics, and other relevant stakeholders. Compiled by academics at King’s College London and partners from the UK’s Nuclear Security Capacity Building Programme (NSCBP), the NSBB provides a comprehensive and objective overview of the international nuclear security framework and its evolution. The authors are grateful for the continuing support of the Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) which has enabled the book’s publication and updating, with the NSBB freely available in digital form. The NSBB offers contextual information on nuclear and radioactive materials to explain the nature of the threat, and examines international agreements and guidance considered by the authors to be most relevant to nuclear security. The NSBB also serves as a comprehensive reference manual by consolidating the texts of key international instruments, conventions, and informal initiatives. The latest version of the NSBB builds on previous iterations, while also reflecting on latest developments in the field. This includes the aftermath of the NSS process and recent international convening events for nuclear security, such as the Conference of the Parties to the Amendment to the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material in 2022 and the International Conference on Nuclear Security (ICONS) in 2024. Since the last iteration of the NSBB, all original texts cited in full have been checked for updates, and new documents of relevance have been added. The authors adopt the definition of ‘nuclear security’ applied by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA): ‘The prevention and detection of, and response to, theft, sabotage, unauthorized access, illegal transfer or other malicious acts involving nuclear material, other radioactive substances or their associated facilities’. Liderul organizației teritoriale a Partidului Socialiștilor a anunțat într-o conferință de presă că a luat această decizie întrucât nu cunoaște „limba moldovenească”, în contextul în care noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral, adoptate în august, obligă candidații să cunoască limbile română și găgăuză.

La o conferință de presă susținută alături de liderul partidului, Igor Dodon, parlamentarul a acuzat majoritatea parlamentară că a modificat intenționat, cu puțin timp înainte de alegeri, Codul electoral, introducând o normă care limitează participarea la scrutin a persoanelor care nu vorbesc limba de stat.
Am luat decizia de a nu-mi depune candidatura la alegerile pentru funcția de bașcan”, a declarat Uzun, care a criticat noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral.
Igor Dodon a mai declarat, că modificarea legislației electorale cu doar două săptămâni înainte de perioada electorală este contrară Constituției și practicilor europene.
Condiția privind cunoașterea limbii trebuia să fie introdusă începând cu următorul ciclu electoral, peste patru ani”, a afirmat Dodon.
Scrutinele se vor desfășura după noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral al Republicii Moldova, întrucât Codul Electoral al autonomiei nu mai este valabil.
În listele electorale din regiune sunt înscriși în jur de 129.000 de alegători.

Source: screen grab from RFE/RL's Georgian Service video Home / News / Amid Brawls and Protests, CEC Announces Final Results, Stamps GD Victory News Amid Brawls and Protests, CEC Announces Final Results, Stamps GD Victory Civil.ge Send an email 17/11/2024 - 11:13 4 minutes read Facebook X LinkedIn Reddit Pocket Skype Messenger Messenger WhatsApp Telegram Viber Share via Email Print On November 16, Georgia’s Central Election Commission (CEC) announced the final summary protocol of the October 26 parliamentary elections, effectively stamping nearly 54 percent-victory for the ruling Georgian Dream party. But with the elections widely considered by the opposition and observers to have been rigged, the CEC meeting was marred by brawls and citizens protested outside the building. Shortly after the start of the meeting, Davit Kirtadze , the representative of the opposition Unity-UNM in the CEC, confronted the CEC Chair, Giorgi Kalandarishvili , calling him a “black spot” and splashing black paint on his face. This act was apparently a reference to the alleged violation of the ballot secrecy in the elections, in particular the issue of thin ballot papers which made it visible from the outside which party a citizen was voting for. Davit Kirtadze (Unity-UNM representative) splashes black paint on Giorgi Kalandarishvili, CEC Chair; Photo: Screen grab from RFE/RL Georgian Service video “You are the shame of our country and you are the black spot,” Kirtadze told Kalandarishvili. Kalandarishvili had to call a break. The meeting resumed after half an hour. CEC Chair Kalandarishvili returned wearing an eye patch. The number of voters who participated in the elections was 2,111,834.

“The most special and important thing is that the political parties that have won mandates as a result of the voters’ participation in the elections ensure their respect and due recognition of their choice,” said CEC Chairman Giorgi Kalandarishvili as he signed and stamped the official, albeit controversial, results.

“The Georgian Parliament will meet on November 25,” Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze told journalists on November 25, although he said he does not expect Salome Zurabishvili to convene the first session.

The CEC clarified that voter registration centers in the West Bank will open its doors Saturday morning, August 15, 2026, for a period of 5 days, to be closed on Wednesday evening, August 19, 2026. Concerning the nomination stage, submission of nomination applications will be open on Saturday morning, September 26, 2026, for a period of 12 days, and shall be closed on Wednesday evening, October 7, 2026. Meanwhile, electoral campaigning will be launched starting Friday, November 6, 2026, for a period of 21 days. Electoral campaigning activities shall be halted – electoral silence/blackout, on Friday, November 27, 2026. Early voting for members of security forces will be conducted on November 26, 2026, whereas polling day for the general public will be Saturday, November 28, 2026. Preliminary results of the elections are planned to be announced within 24 hours of its preparation, however, final results will be published within two weeks of polling day, after concluding all legal challenges and appeals of the results, in accordance with the law. Dispute over electoral reforms heats up as Georgian election looms Log In News Stories In Focus Opinion and Editorial Newsletters Culture Daily Brief Advertise with Us About Us Jobs Charles Michel Agreement Dispute over electoral reforms heats up as Georgian election looms by Shota Kincha • 5 min read Share ▲ Parliamentary elections 2020.
A dispute over electoral reforms is heating up in Georgia ahead of crucial local elections, the result of which will determine if snap parliamentary elections follow in 2022.
On 18 June, the Council of Europe’s Venice Commission and OSCE’s Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) published a joint opinion on the election code amendment bill.

Transparent staffing of electoral commissions According to the revised draft amendment, the CEC, the top management body of the Electoral Administration, is to be composed of 17 members including the chair, instead of the current 12, and to include at least seven non-partisan members with a maximum of nine from political parties.
Electoral reforms were a part of an EU-brokered agreement in April to end the political impasse between the government and opposition parties.
As part of the agreement, Georgian Dream also committed to calling the early parliamentary elections if they won less than 43% of proportional votes.
While this was not explicitly mentioned in the April deal, several opposition groups have insisted this is a precondition to gain public trust in the upcoming local elections slated for October.
Following the parliamentary vote last autumn, Zhvania and the CEC were accused of electoral fraud, which was followed by all opposition groups boycotting the new parliament for months.
The OSCE/ODIHR observation mission did not question the legitimacy of the final electoral outcome.
Electoral changes are only a part of the dispute.

[Read more on OC Media : Amnesty controversy threatens to derail EU-brokered deal in Georgia ] ‘A demonstration of force’ To implement the electoral reforms promised in the agreement, Georgian Dream initially tabled a draft in March, and resubmitted it in May together with Citizens and European Socialists, opposition groups that took up their seats in parliament as early as January.

However, parliament’s electoral reform task force still lacks inclusivity as unlike smaller parties, the UNM-dominated bloc that garnered 36 seats in the 150-member parliament, have refused to sign the April deal, even after ending their parliamentary boycott in May.

While the April agreement effectively dismantled the already shaky opposition front that had earlier vowed to jointly force Georgian Dream to call the snap elections, most opposition groups remain critical of how the governing party plans to proceed with the reforms.

The Venice Commission and ODIHR underlined the need for more robust transparency in staffing non-partisan members, a call that reflected criticism by most watchdogs and opposition groups that in recent years have described the non-partisan members as frequently lobbying for or being biased in favour of the ruling party.

Photo: Mariam Nikuradze/OC Media Most electoral reform advocates support the idea of staffing the CEC with only non-partisan, ‘professional’ members in the future but also consider it unrealistic to do so immediately.

On 15 June, election watchdog group ISFED underlined that for the sake of transparency, the special selection committee should be obliged to justify their choices for ‘professional’ CEC membership candidacies.

In the recent elections, local observers have highlighted the problems caused by a heavy presence of party activists outside polling stations, something they argue increases the risks of voter control and intimidation.

For the upcoming election, the authorities are mulling introducing some electronic voting technologies, possibly including poll pads to check in voters, electronic voting machines, and facial recognition devices.
However, so far, Georgia lacks the legal framework to regulate the application of these technologies as well as enough time before the election to widely integrate them in the voting process.

Charles Michel Agreement 2021 Georgian Local Elections Georgia Shota Kincha • Follow 411 articles • 0 Followers After fleeing a not-so-promising academic career and a disastrous attempt at being a bisexual activist, Shota is now a grumpy staff writer covering Georgia-related topics at OC Media.
He focuses on nationalism, far-right movements, gender, and queer issues, with an eye on Eastern and Central Europe.
Since the 2020 parliamentary elections, Georgia has experienced political deadlock.
Following weeks of internal debates and almost 14 months after 2020’s parliamentary elections, leading UNM member Khatia Dekanoidze announced the decision on Monday.

The dual vote will coincide with elections for the People’s Assembly of Gagauzia (APG), the autonomous region's legislature. Central authorities intervened under the Electoral Code after local deputies failed to set a date during three consecutive sessions on August 17, August 26, and September 1, with the final attempt collapsing due to a lack of quorum. Statutory deadlines and institutional intervention Under Moldovan law, regional snap elections must take place within three months of an executive vacancy, with the date formally established at least 80 days before polling day. When local authorities fail to meet statutory deadlines, the Central Electoral Commission (CEC) is legally empowered to set the date at least 75 days prior to the ballot. “The commission recommended scheduling the election for November 15, the same date set for the People’s Assembly vote,” said CEC Deputy Chairman Pavel Postica during Tuesday's commission meeting. “The People’s Assembly was notified that failing an agreement within statutory deadlines, the central authority would step in. We received no response prior to this decision.” The office of the governor, traditionally known as the Bashkan, became vacant following the final criminal conviction of Evghenia Guțul, who was sentenced to seven years in prison for illegal financing related to the outlawed Șor Party. Comrat regional authorities formally acknowledged the vacancy on August 17. tool.excerpt: Electrical transformer explosion triggers deadly fire in Phuket, killing 11 - tl;dr daily news Briefing World U.S. Business Technology Entertainment Sports Search... ⌘K Search Login Home world Electrical transformer explosion triggers deadly fire in Phuket, killing 11 November 16, 2026 at 09:45 AM • 3 min read • Source: Al Jazeera Photo: Al Jazeera TL;DR A fire in a mixed-use building in Patong, Phuket, killed 11 people and injured others early Monday. Authorities attribute the blaze to an exploding electrical transformer, which ignited combustible materials in a ground-floor motorcycle shop. The incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding building safety in Thai tourist hubs, following a similar mass-casualty fire in Bangkok in July. Key points At least 11 people died and 16 to 30 others were injured in a fire at a building in Patong, Phuket, starting around 2:00-3:17 AM local time. The building housed a restaurant, rented accommodation, and a motorcycle rental shop on the ground floor, which stored approximately 100 motorcycles, gas, engine oil, and plastic materials. Police and officials ruled out arson, citing an exploding electrical transformer near the building as the likely cause, which ignited the combustible materials and produced thick, toxic smoke. Victims were found on the third, fourth, and fifth floors, indicating they attempted to escape upward due to smoke blocking lower exits; no tourists were among the dead or injured. This is the second major fire causing mass casualties in Thailand since July, when a Bangkok bar fire killed about 40 people due to an electrical short circuit. Background Thailand has faced scrutiny over health and safety regulations in commercial and entertainment venues. In 2012, a fire in a Phuket club killed four people, and in 2009, a Bangkok club fire during New Year celebrations killed 67. The July 2026 Bangkok bar fire, which killed approximately 40, intensified calls for stricter enforcement of safety standards in crowded public spaces. How outlets are covering it Al Jazeera and AP News report 16 and 17 injured, respectively, while Thai PBS World states over 30 were injured, primarily from smoke inhalation. All sources agree on the 11 fatalities and the transformer explosion as the cause. The CEC clarified that voter registration centers in the West Bank will open its doors Saturday morning, August 15, 2026, for a period of 5 days, to be closed on Wednesday evening, August 19, 2026. Concerning the nomination stage, submission of nomination applications will be open on Saturday morning, September 26, 2026, for a period of 12 days, and shall be closed on Wednesday evening, October 7, 2026. Meanwhile, electoral campaigning will be launched starting Friday, November 6, 2026, for a period of 21 days. Electoral campaigning activities shall be halted – electoral silence/blackout, on Friday, November 27, 2026. Early voting for members of security forces will be conducted on November 26, 2026, whereas polling day for the general public will be Saturday, November 28, 2026. Preliminary results of the elections are planned to be announced within 24 hours of its preparation, however, final results will be published within two weeks of polling day, after concluding all legal challenges and appeals of the results, in accordance with the law. Meanwhile, electoral campaigning will be launched starting Friday, November 6, 2026, for a period of 21 days. Electoral campaigning activities shall be halted – electoral silence/blackout, on Friday, November 27, 2026. Early voting for members of security forces will be conducted on November 26, 2026, whereas polling day for the general public will be Saturday, November 28, 2026. Preliminary results of the elections are planned to be announced within 24 hours of its preparation, however, final results will be published within two weeks of polling day, after concluding all legal challenges and appeals of the results, in accordance with the law. sentences: The fire followed the explosion of a transformer in front of a townhouse project across from the Ocean View Phuket Hotel on Sirirat Road, which runs from Patong to Karon.
Here in Phuket, transformer explosions, electrocutions and blackouts are generally accepted as regular weekly occurrences.
Roadside noodle vendor Kanjana Sonjai, 29, said, “My aunt and I were making noodles next to the transformer at about 2pm when it suddenly exploded.

Staff of the nearby JR Massage shop, located in the shophouse complex behind the transformer, said smaller explosions were heard at 8am and again at 10am, after which electricians arrived to make repairs.
However, staff at Patong Municipality’s Division of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation said they were only informed of the fire at around 2.30pm and arrived within five minutes.
Within seconds the entire noodle cart was engulfed in flames.” ADVERTISEMENT Her aunt is now being treated at Patong Hospital, Ms Kanjana said.
It was the third and largest of three explosions from electrical equipment on the same concrete support structure today, local residents said.
A laundress who operates a shop nearby said the repairmen left at about 1pm; then the transformer gave off smoke until it suddenly blew up and burst into flames.
Although the fire was reported immediately, it took firefighters over an hour to arrive, she said.
Six motorbikes and a Honda Jazz were damaged by the fire.
It took 14 officers with three fire trucks about 20 minutes to extinguish the flames, after which they cut off the power supply to the pole, they said.
Although it was more than 250 years ago that Benjamin Franklin flew his kite, provincial Thailand has yet to develop any credibility in the effective or safe management of electricity.

Phuket Island is connected by the Sarasin Bridge to Phang Nga province to the north. The next nearest province is Krabi, to the east across Phang Nga Bay. tool.excerpt: Moldova sets Gagauzia governor vote for Nov. 15 amid local deadlock News Programs • Live Search Search News Programs • Live Elections Moldova sets Gagauzia governor vote for Nov. 15 amid local deadlock Published 02.09.2026 06:57 Moldova’s Central Electoral Commission stepped in on Tuesday to schedule regional elections in Gagauzia for Nov. 15, breaking a local legislative deadlock following the final conviction of former governor Evghenia Guțul. The dual vote will coincide with elections for the People’s Assembly of Gagauzia (APG), the autonomous region's legislature. tool.title: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami
tool.excerpt: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami. The tsunami generated by the Sumatra earthquake on December 26, 2004 affected many countries around the Indian Ocean and Thailand also suffered severely from this event, i.e. 6 provinces along the Andaman coastline. More than 8,000 people perished or went missing, 4,500 houses were totally destroyed, and economic losses were estimated at more than 14 billion baht. Since it bore the brunt of the tidal wave at its peak, Phang Nga experienced the largest number of fatalities or missing (more than 65%) as well as property damage (about 50%). The Government was prominent in several short- and long-term measures following the disaster management cycle, including the development of a tsunami resilient community. This paper discusses several measures implemented by the government, private sectors, and international organizations.

tool.title: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami
tool.excerpt: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami. The tsunami generated by the Sumatra earthquake on December 26, 2004 affected many countries around the Indian Ocean and Thailand also suffered severely from this event, i.e. 6 provinces along the Andaman coastline. More than 8,000 people perished or went missing, 4,500 houses were totally destroyed, and economic losses were estimated at more than 14 billion baht. Since it bore the brunt of the tidal wave at its peak, Phang Nga experienced the largest number of fatalities or missing (more than 65%) as well as property damage (about 50%). The Government was prominent in several short- and long-term measures following the disaster management cycle, including the development of a tsunami resilient community. This paper discusses several measures implemented by the government, private sectors, and international organizations.

tool.title: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami
tool.excerpt: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami. The tsunami generated by the Sumatra earthquake on December 26, 2004 affected many countries around the Indian Ocean and Thailand also suffered severely from this event, i.e. 6 provinces along the Andaman coastline. More than 8,000 people perished or went missing, 4,500 houses were totally destroyed, and economic losses were estimated at more than 14 billion baht. Since it bore the brunt of the tidal wave at its peak, Phang Nga experienced the largest number of fatalities or missing (more than 65%) as well as property damage (about 50%). The Government was prominent in several short- and long-term measures following the disaster management cycle, including the development of a tsunami resilient community. This paper discusses several measures implemented by the government, private sectors, and international organizations.

tool.title: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami
tool.excerpt: Recovery Process in Thailand after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami. The tsunami generated by the Sumatra earthquake on December 26, 2004 affected many countries around the Indian Ocean and Thailand also suffered severely from this event, i.e. 6 provinces along the Andaman coastline. More than 8,000 people perished or went missing, 4,500 houses were totally destroyed, and economic losses were estimated at more than 14 billion baht. Since it bore the brunt of the tidal wave at its peak, Phang Nga experienced the largest number of fatalities or missing (more than 65%) as well as property damage (about 50%). The Government was prominent in several short- and long-term measures following the disaster management cycle, including the development of a tsunami resilient community. This paper discusses several measures implemented by the government, private sectors, and international organizations.
